yt_upper_canyon.blurb: Upper Canyon is one of three sections of the Rock Gardens, a small granite crag right beside Whitehorse. It holds about fourteen short routes, nearly all of them bolted, with a couple of trad lines mixed in. Grades start around 5.8 and climb to 5.12, with the bulk of the lines in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, so there is a fair amount for newer leaders and a few hard tests besides. Walls catch the sun in the afternoon, and the canyon can be buggy in warm weather. Because it is so close to town it sees more traffic than most Yukon cliffs, though it is quieter than neighbouring Grand Central Station.

_expect.name: The Elephant Head - South Face (aka Hyperion Slab)

ca_the_elephant_head_south_face_aka_hype.blurb: Hyperion Slab is the broad south side of the Elephant Head, the first big formation met when walking into Texas Canyon in the Angeles National Forest, north of Los Angeles. A low-angle slab with a roof near its base, it offers around fourteen routes, almost all bolted, from very easy up to 5.11. The largest share sit in the 5.10 range, with a spread of easier 5.6 to 5.9 lines for those who want a gentler outing, and some climbs run two pitches up the face. Bolts can be widely spaced on the upper slab. Conglomerate here breaks easily when damp, so it is a place for dry days only.

ar_fern_gulley.blurb: Fern Gulley is a sheltered little ravine on the Invasion cliff line in the Cowell and Deer part of north-central Arkansas, with a damp, almost rainforest atmosphere. It packs thirteen problems and routes into a small space: seven boulder problems running from V2 up to V7, and six bolted sport routes between 5.10 and 5.12. Nothing here is aimed at beginners, and the neighbouring Invasion Area has the same steep, demanding bent. It is a good stop for climbers who already lead around 5.10 and up, or who are looking for a short session of harder sandstone bouldering.

ar_arachnophobia_dark_side_international.blurb: This stretch of the West Main Bluff at Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas gathers three adjoining walls into one trad-focused section. Thirteen routes range from 5.8 to 5.12, with most clustered at 5.9 to 5.11, so mid-grade climbers will find plenty to do. The wall begins near the Dog Walkdown, with big roofs at its left end, and carries on toward the zone around Razorback Roof. Expect traditional gear routes on solid sandstone, including finger- and fist-sized cracks and a few roof problems. The main bluff faces west, which suits cooler months and summer mornings.

ar_moondye_boulder.blurb: Moondye is a single sandstone boulder within the Idaho Boulders zone at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas. It sits at the south end of the northern cluster, a little downhill from a sport route, and carries thirteen problems. Difficulty skews hard: there is a lone easy warm-up around V0, a handful from V2 to V6, and the rest stretch from V8 through the double digits, topping out near V12 on a long traverse. The top-out is an easy walk-off on the north side. Neighbouring boulders sit close together, so moving between problems is easy.

ar_coup_d_etat_wall.blurb: Coup D'etat Wall forms the right-hand end of the West Main Bluff at Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas. Thirteen routes are spread from 5.5 to 5.12: mostly crack climbs placed with trad gear, plus a few bolted face lines that carry the harder grades. The core of the wall is at 5.10, with a smaller group of easier pitches and a few hard sport lines above 5.11. It is a short hike up to the base, and the sandstone gives a mix of thin cracks and some excellent face climbing. Stronger leaders looking for classic Arkansas crack work will feel at home here.

ar_magoo_rock.blurb: Magoo Rock is a free-standing block on the east side of the canyon at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, tucked just west of the Roman Wall. About nine bolted sport routes share it with a few boulder problems. Most leads fall in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, with a couple of easier 5.7s and a single 5.11, so it suits climbers who are comfortable at 5.9. Boulder problems run from V1 to V6. The sandstone is covered in features and has some of the biggest jugs found anywhere at the ranch, which makes it a pleasant, juggy outing.
